Added 2026-07-14 (plan 1.2.B). FUT2 Ile129Ser missense variant (rs602662), position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr19:49206985, G>A, gene on plus strand). Hazra et al. 2008 GWAS (PMID 18776911, n>45000, p=6.5e-10) found the A allele associated with HIGHER plasma vitamin B12 (effect -0.08 SD per reference G allele). CAVEAT: this SNP is in strong LD with the FUT2 secretor/non-secretor haplotype (rs601338 W143X nonsense variant); the serum-B12 association partly reflects haptocorrin-binding/glycosylation differences by secretor status (PMID 29040465) rather than pure tissue-level B12 status, so a high score here should be read as 'FUT2 genotype associated with higher measured serum B12', not necessarily 'better B12 nutritional status'. Non-secretor status (same haplotype) also affects gut microbiota composition and H. pylori/norovirus susceptibility - out of scope for this row.

Added 2026-08-05 (plan 1.2.C). TCN1 Asp301Tyr missense variant (rs34324219), position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr11:59623378, C>A forward strand). Grarup et al. 2013 PLoS Genetics deep-sequencing GWAS of vitamin B12/folate (PMID 23754956, combined p=1.1e-111, effect=0.21 SD) found the C allele associated with HIGHER serum B12, same direction convention as the existing FUT2 row (effect_allele = allele associated with higher B12, not a disease-risk allele). TCN1 encodes transcobalamin-1/haptocorrin, the major B12-binding protein in saliva and gastric juice - functionally distinct from FUT2 (secretor status) and from TCN2 (the transporter that actually delivers B12 into cells), so this SNP adds an independent, non-redundant signal to the trait rather than re-measuring the same mechanism.

Added 2026-08-05 (plan 1.2.C). CUBN Phe253Ser/Cys/Tyr missense variant (rs1801222), position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr10:17156151, A>G forward strand — A is the major/reference allele on dbSNP; the source GWAS labelled it the 'effect' allele, so effect_allele=A here follows the paper's convention, not dbSNP's ref/alt labelling). Grarup et al. 2013 PLoS Genetics (PMID 23754956, combined p=3.3e-75, effect=0.11 SD) found the A allele associated with HIGHER serum B12, same direction convention as the existing FUT2/TCN1 rows. CUBN encodes cubilin, the intestinal receptor (with amnionless) required to absorb the intrinsic-factor/B12 complex in the terminal ileum - a distinct absorption-stage mechanism from FUT2 (binding-protein glycosylation) and TCN1 (transport-protein levels), so this SNP is functionally independent of the other two rows in this trait_category. Weight set lower than TCN1/FUT2 to reflect its smaller per-allele effect size (0.11 vs 0.21/-0.08 SD).

Added 2026-07-14 (plan 1.2.B). HFE H63D (p.His63Asp, rs1799945), position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr6:26091179, C>G, gene on plus strand). Second major HFE hemochromatosis variant, discovered alongside C282Y (rs1800562, already in this panel) in Feder et al. 1996 (PMID 8696333). G/G homozygotes and C282Y/H63D compound heterozygotes carry elevated iron-overload risk, though penetrance is substantially lower than C282Y homozygosity - weight set below the existing C282Y row (0.30) to reflect this. Same trait_category as rs1800562 so the two combine; note the existing rs1800562 row's effect_allele/risk_genotype pairing (G effect_allele vs A/A risk_genotype) looks internally inconsistent and was NOT re-verified as part of this task - flagged as a follow-up, not fixed here.

Added 2026-07-14 (plan 1.2.B). ADORA2A intronic variant, position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr22:24837301, T>C, gene on plus strand). Alsene et al. 2003 (PMID 12825092) found the T allele predisposes to caffeine-induced anxiety (T/T carriers show the strongest anxiogenic response); replicated in a 2019 systematic review (PMID 31817803). New trait_category (separate from 'Caffeine metabolism' CYP1A2/AHR rows, which capture metabolic speed, not subjective sensitivity) - intended to complement those rows with a sensitivity axis. CAVEAT: literature also links the C allele (opposite allele) to caffeine-induced sleep disturbance/insomnia - a distinct sub-phenotype this row's direction does not capture; only the better-replicated anxiety association is scored here.

Added 2026-07-14 (plan 1.2.B). HNMT Thr105Ile (rs11558538), position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr2:138759649, C>T, gene on plus strand). Added 2026-07-14 (plan 1.2.B). COL1A1 Sp1 binding-site polymorphism (rs1800012), position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr17:48277749, C>A forward strand; COL1A1 is on the MINUS strand, so the forward-strand C/A pair corresponds to the classical transcript-relative G/T 'S/s' nomenclature used in the literature - S=G=C(fwd)=major/protective, s=T=A(fwd)=minor/risk). Mann & Ralston 2003 meta-analysis (PMID 12810179) found the minor 's' allele (A on forward strand) associated with lower bone mineral density and increased osteoporotic fracture risk (largest effect for vertebral fracture). Complements the existing LRP5/TNFRSF11B rows in this trait_category.

Added 2026-07-14 (plan 1.2.B). CLOCK 3111T/C polymorphism (rs1801260), position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr4:56301369, A>G forward strand; CLOCK is on the MINUS strand, so forward-strand A/G corresponds to the classical transcript-relative T/C nomenclature - T=A(fwd)=major, C=G(fwd)=minor/evening-preference allele). Mishima et al. 2005 (PMID 15578592) and earlier Katzenberg et al. 1998 found the C allele (=G on forward strand) associated with EVENING preference, i.e. the OPPOSITE direction from this row's trait_category (which scores 'morning/early-bird' positively via the PER2 rs2304672 row already present) - effect_direction set to '-' so the two SNPs combine correctly (more evening-allele copies lowers the early-bird score). CAVEAT: replication across populations has been inconsistent for this SNP specifically.

Added 2026-07-14 (plan 1.2.B). rs4343, position/alleles verified against dbSNP GRCh37 (chr17:61566031, G>A, gene on plus strand).
